evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skipped the framing entirely. Went from greeting/contact verification directly to logistics. No time-boxed ask or promise of a dependable quote, and no wait for customer confirmation before probing.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' Customer raised no unprompted concerns; rep moved straight to logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns raised by customer, so no follow-up gap.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apt), floor (2nd to 1st), rooms (1 bed), walking distance (clarified ~bus and a half = ~50 feet), special items (TV, standing desk, dresser, TV stand, rattan chair, many boxes/containers), additional stops (none), parking details (clarified for both locations). All seven items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep never asked 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' — customer is packing themselves, but offer was never made.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes. Rep asked 'typical block count for a move the size is about fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you feel like you fall within that range?' Customer responded they'd be in the 25–40 range.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial. Rep gave a time-range anchor ('between two and a half and three and a half hours') but never gave a price anchor or range (e.g., '$XXX–$XXX for this move'). The pricing framing discusses minimums and increments, but no actual dollar estimate was provided.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. Rep covered: two-and-a-half-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, clock starts on arrival, pricing model ('prorated in the fifteen minute increments'), 60¢/lb coverage, and payment timing (due at end of move, no deposit). No trip fee or packing materials were disclosed (N/A, as packing wasn't offered).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. No 'Does that feel fair?' was asked, and no pause offered for the customer to react to pricing.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. Rep stated: 'we do have our on time guarantee we value your time. So, if we can't make it in, in a time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. Rep stated: 'we do have that no worries, damage coverage which is our free evaluation coverage included in the hourly rate provides up to $2,000 per move to repair replace or reimburse for accidental damages and that's on top of the 60¢ per pound coverage.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Rep never asked 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Customer did ask about deposits/payment during this section, and rep answered, but the Two Promises section was not closed with a confirmatory question.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. Rep asked 'Do you have any questions for me?' — the empty, automatic 'any questions' version, not 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Rep never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or a comparable catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any recognizable variant. Call ended with 'Have a good rest of your day and good luck with your move' — a pleasant close but no ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: True. Rep stated 'no deposit required to get on the schedule' and 'no she change fees or oh, my goodness the Friday no charges or fees to change the time or reschedule anything like, that.' This functionally conveys no-penalty commitment to the rate, though not in the exact 'rate lock' terminology.

top_strength: Brianne gathered complete logistics details (property types, floors, walking distances, special items, box counts) with natural curiosity and real-world rapport—the standing-desk conversation felt genuine and built trust.
coaching_note: Section 1 must open with the quid pro quo (time-boxed promise + dependable quote + wait for yes) before any probing starts; Section 7 must close with an explicit ask for the business ('Would you like our help with your move?') rather than ending with well-wishes alone—without it, no sale is captured even if the customer is ready.
